AUTHOR: Bürgi
TITLE: Automated counting of fish in moving diver-operated videos (DOV) for biodiversity assessments
SPECIES: Epinephelus marginatus, Sciaena umbra, Diplodus vulgaris
DATA: Own diver-operated GoPro transect videos (125 m2), 2022, cold and warm season; 55 videos used for counting; detector data from Bürgi et al. 2024 (Dryad)
V_EV: Sec 2.1: 'The depth ranged from 1 to 37 m, and data were collected in 2022 at different times of the year (cold and warm season).'
D2: Video-level train/validation/test (7 videos moved train->validation; 5 high-abundance videos moved train->test; Table S2)
D_EV: Sec 2.2.1: 'We moved seven videos from the training to the validation set... five videos with the highest occurrence rates were removed from the training and incorporated into the test set.'
R_EV: Sec 2.1: all videos from the same 2022 Mediterranean DOV campaign; test set held out from same dataset.
C_EV: Sec 3.2: 'we found the best performing confidence threshold based on the respective f1 score on the validation set... 0.55 for E. marginatus, 0.60 for S. umbra and 0.45 for D. vulgaris.'
E_EV: Sec 2.2.2: 'A marine biology expert counted the actual fish abundance/count (True FishAbundance) per video, resulting in a groundtruth count per video.'
ARCH: Modified YOLOv7 detector + per-video count aggregation via Nmax, 1D k-means (NCluster), NHeuristic, Temporal Convolutional Network (NTCN)
METR: mAP, F1 (detector); absolute error, absolute percentage error, Pearson correlation vs expert counts
NOTE: Counting methods (NCluster/NHeuristic/NTCN vs Nmax) explicitly address double counting/undercounting in moving-camera video -> C5 duplicate handling; false-positive counts in zero-occurrence videos also reported. E1 = Nmax plus abundance per video. Reference = expert count of same videos (inter-operator CV 0-32%). Habitat type not stated (ENV=NR). Detector originally from Bürgi et al. 2024 with modified splits.
